subject: BCP & Resilience: RTO/RPO SLAs, Failback Sequencing, and Audit Evidence
messages:
From: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@northstar.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@northstar.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: RTO/RPO commitments, failback sequencing and evidence

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team appreciated the latency and cost detail. Northstar’s Compliance & Resilience team has a few follow-ups for the procurement packet:

1) Can you provide committed RTO and RPO targets for Hosted API, Dedicated pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments? Please indicate whether those are contractual SLAs or operational commitments.

2) We need a short sequencing-runbook that explains multi-region failover and failback behavior (including KV cache handling, in-flight requests, and recommended client retry semantics).

3) Evidence: do you have recent DR test artifacts (runbooks exercised, dated test logs, post-mortem summaries) and the relevant SOC2/audit references we can attach to our RFP response?

Timing: Northstar is finalizing vendor selection by 11/20. If you can share an assurance matrix + any evidence by next week that would be ideal.

Appreciate it — can set up a 30-min technical Q&A if helpful.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Miller
Head of Resilience, Northstar Financial
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miller <jordan.miller@northstar.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@northstar.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-07T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: RTO/RPO commitments, failback sequencing and evidence

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is an initial assurance matrix (redwood-bcp-assurance-matrix-v1.xlsx) that summarizes target RTO/RPO by deployment type and the operational controls we use to meet them. High-level bullets below — happy to walk through in a quick call: 

- Hosted API: Target RTO 15 minutes for control-plane incidents (regional restarts); RPO best-effort (stateless request model). Not an SLA for stateful workloads unless using Dedicated with prefix caching.
- Dedicated pools: SLA-backed 99.9% availability for reserved capacity; RTO target 5 minutes for autoscale policy adjustments or rapid instance replacement (dependent on instance type). Typical RPO < 30s for KV/prefix cached sessions when using our managed session layer.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): We provide operational runbooks and assisted failover patterns; SLA terms are contract-negotiable. RTO/RPO depend on customer topology; our recommended config supports RTO < 30 minutes and RPO configurable to < 1 minute with cross-region replication.

Failback sequencing (summary): 
- Step 1 — Route new traffic to recovery region while preserving KV caches where available.
- Step 2 — Drain in-flight requests from primary region using connection draining and client-aware retry semantics (exponential backoff + idempotency tokens).
- Step 3 — Rehydrate caches from persisted prefix/KV snapshots; reconcile stream offsets for embeddings/indices.
- Step 4 — Run consistency checks, smoke tests, then gradually shift traffic back (canaries -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%).

Attachments in this message: redwood-bcp-assurance-matrix-v1.xlsx (matrix), rto-rpo-evidence-summary.pdf (summary of test artifacts and SOC2 references). We will follow up with the underlying test logs.

If Northstar wants, Marcus can join a technical call next week to cover Dedicated pool SLA language and the exact test artifacts we can provide.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

- Smoke tests: 3 rounds passed; latency regression < 5% compared to baseline.

We redacted customer-identifying logs and included checksums for each file in the ZIP. Also adding a short README inside the ZIP describing the mapping from log names to systems.

If Legal flags anything, let me know and I can rerun the artifact export with tighter anonymization.
